query: Create a report evaluating observatory conditions using the Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI) and identifying stations meeting Optimal Observing Window (OOW) criteria. The output should group stations by whether meets OOW (bool:True or False). For each group, you should provide its boolean value of OOW, the count of stations, average AOI (rounded to 3 decimal places) and a JSON array whose elements each include  `station` (observatory name), `aoi` (AOI value), `lunar_factors` object with `stage` (lunar stage) and `distance` (lunar distance), and `solar_status` (solar status).
sol_sql: SELECT is_optimal_window, COUNT(*) AS station_count, ROUND(AVG(aoi), 3) AS avg_aoi, JSON_GROUP_ARRAY(JSON_OBJECT( 'station', ObservStation, 'aoi', ROUND(aoi, 3), 'lunar_factors', JSON_OBJECT( 'stage', LunarStage, 'distance', LunarDistDeg ), 'solar_status', SolarStatus )) AS observatory_details FROM ( SELECT o.ObservStation, o.AtmosTransparency * (1 - o.HumidityRate/100) * (1 - 0.02 * o.WindSpeedMs) AS aoi, o.LunarStage, o.LunarDistDeg, o.SolarStatus, CASE WHEN o.AtmosTransparency * (1 - o.HumidityRate/100) * (1 - 0.02 * o.WindSpeedMs) > 0.85 AND (o.LunarStage = 'New' OR o.LunarStage = 'First Quarter') AND o.LunarDistDeg > 45 AND (o.SolarStatus = 'Low' OR o.SolarStatus = 'Moderate') THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_optimal_window FROM Observatories o ) GROUP BY is_optimal_window;

Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).description: Combines SNR and noise floor to provide a unified signal quality metric.
Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI).definition: $\text{SNQI} = \text{SnrRatio} - 0.1 \times |\text{NoiseFloorDbm}|$, where higher values indicate better detection quality. Positive values generally indicate analyzable signals.

Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).description: Quantifies how conducive atmospheric conditions are for signal detection.
Atmospheric Observability Index (AOI).definition: $\text{AOI} = \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{100}) \times (1 - 0.02 \times \text{WindSpeedMs})$, where values closer to 1 indicate ideal observation conditions.

Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).description: Measures the relationship between signal complexity and information density.
Signal Complexity Ratio (SCR).definition: $\text{SCR} = \frac{\text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{InfoDense}}{\log(\text{BwHz})}$, where higher values suggest potential artificial origin rather than natural phenomena.

Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.description: Combines multiple factors to estimate likelihood of technological origin.
Technological Origin Likelihood Score (T.definition: $\text{TOLS} = \text{TechSigProb} \times (1 - \text{NatSrcProb}) \times \text{SigUnique} \times (0.5 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{10})$, where values above 0.75 warrant further investigation as potential technosignatures.

Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).description: Measures the proportion of bandwidth to center frequency, helping identify signal type.
Bandwidth-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 10^6}$, where narrow ratios ($<0.001$) often indicate technological signals while wider ratios suggest natural phenomena.

Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.description: Calculates the effective sensitivity of the detection setup based on telescope and environmental factors.
Detection Instrument Sensitivity Factor.definition: $\text{DISF} = (10 - \frac{|\text{AirTempC} - 15|}{10}) \times \text{AtmosTransparency} \times (1 - \frac{\text{HumidityRate}}{200}) \times \frac{100 - \text{LunarDistDeg}}{100}$, where values closer to 10 indicate optimal detection sensitivity.

Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).description: Evaluates the sophistication of potential encoding in the signal.
Encoding Complexity Index (ECI).definition: $\text{ECI} = \frac{\text{CompressRatio} \times \text{ComplexIdx} \times \text{EntropyVal}}{10}$, where values above 1.5 suggest deliberate information encoding rather than random patterns.

Signal Stability Metric (SSM).description: Quantifies overall temporal and spectral stability of a signal.
Signal Stability Metric (SSM).definition: $\text{SSM} = (1 - \frac{|\text{FreqDriftHzs}|}{\text{FreqMhz} \times 1000}) \times \frac{\text{SigDurSec}}{1 + \frac{\text{DoppShiftHz}}{1000}}$, where higher values indicate more stable signals typical of fixed transmitters.

Research Priority Index (RPI).description: Helps researchers prioritize signals for follow-up based on multiple factors.
Research Priority Index (RPI).definition: $\text{RPI} = (\text{TechSigProb} \times 4 + \frac{\text{BioSigProb}}{100} + \text{SigUnique} \times 2 + \frac{\text{AnomScore}}{2}) \times (1 - \text{FalsePosProb})$, where values above 3 indicate high research priority.

Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).description: Calculates the potential interference from lunar illumination on observations.
Lunar Interference Factor (LIF).definition: $\text{LIF} = (1 - \frac{\text{LunarDistDeg}}{180}) \times (1 - \text{AtmosTransparency})$, where higher values indicate more lunar interference. Values above 0.5 suggest significant lunar contamination in data.

Technosignature.description: Defines the concept of signals that indicate technological activity.
Technosignature.definition: A signal with $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.7$, $\text{NatSrcProb} < 0.3$, and $\text{ArtSrcProb} < 50$ that exhibits narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.001$) and high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 0.8$).

Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).description: Identifies signals showing patterns consistent with deliberate information transmission.
Coherent Information Pattern (CIP).definition: Signals characterized by high signal stability ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$), organized information structure ($\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8), and consistent modulation ($\text{ModType}$ with $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$).

Target of Opportunity (TOO).description: Identifies high-value signals requiring immediate follow-up observation.
Target of Opportunity (TOO).definition: Any signal with $\text{RPI} > 3.5$, $\text{TechSigProb} > 0.8$, and $\text{AnomScore} > 5$ that has not been previously documented or explained by known phenomena.

Optimal Observing Window (OOW).description: Defines conditions when observational quality is maximized.
Optimal Observing Window (OOW).definition: Time periods when $\text{AOI} > 0.85$, $\text{LunarStage}$ is 'New' or 'First Quarter', $\text{LunarDistDeg} > 45$, and $\text{SolarStatus}$ is 'Low' or 'Moderate'.

Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).description: Characterizes situations where signal quality is compromised by environmental factors.
Signal Degradation Scenario (SDS).definition: Observation conditions where one or more of: $\text{AtmosTransparency} < 0.7$, $\text{HumidityRate} > 70$, $\text{WindSpeedMs} > 8$, or $\text{GeomagStatus}$ contains 'Storm', resulting in compromised data quality.

Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).description: Identifies a specific signature associated with technological transmission.
Narrowband Technological Marker (NTM).definition: Signals with extremely narrow bandwidth ($\text{BFR} < 0.0001$), stable frequency ($\text{FreqDriftHzs} < 0.1$).

Observational Confidence Level (OCL).description: Rates the reliability of observations based on conditions and equipment.
Observational Confidence Level (OCL).definition: A classification system with three tiers: 'High' ($\text{AOI} > 0.8$, $\text{EquipStatus} = \text{'Operational'}$, $\text{CalibrStatus} = \text{'Current'}$), 'Medium' ($\text{AOI}$ 0.5-0.8, minor equipment issues), and 'Low' ($\text{AOI} < 0.5$ or significant equipment problems).

Potential Biosignature.description: Defines characteristics of signals potentially associated with biological processes.
Potential Biosignature.definition: Signals with $\text{BioSigProb} > 0.6$, $\text{TechSigProb} < 0.4$, and spectral features that match known biological emission patterns, often associated with specific molecular transitions.

Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).description: Characterizes signals that appear to contain deliberate information encoding.
Encoded Information Transfer (EIT).definition: Signals with $\text{ECI} > 1.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.7 (not random but structured), and consistent internal patterns that suggest language or data encoding schemes.

Fast Radio Transient (FRT).description: Defines a specific class of brief, high-energy radio emissions.
Fast Radio Transient (FRT).definition: Signals with extremely short duration ($\text{SigDurSec} < 0.1$), high signal strength ($\text{SigStrDb} > 15$), broad bandwidth ($\text{BwHz} > 1000000$), and no periodicity ($\text{RepeatCount} = 1$).

WeathProfile: Clear.description: Illustrates optimal weather conditions for signal detection.
WeathProfile: Clear.definition: Indicates pristine sky conditions with no clouds, usually associated with $\text{AtmosTransparency} > 0.9$, low $\text{HumidityRate} (< 40\%)$, and minimal $\text{WindSpeedMs} (< 3.0)$. Provides ideal visibility for optical observations and minimal atmospheric interference for radio observations.

SeeingProfile: Excellent.definition: Describes atmospheric conditions with minimal turbulence, allowing for sharp, detailed observations. Typically corresponds to image stability better than 1 arcsecond and is often associated with stable temperature gradients and low wind speeds ($\text{WindSpeedMs} < 2.5$).

SignalClass: Narrowband.description: Illustrates characteristics of narrowband signal detections.
SignalClass: Narrowband.definition: Describes signals occupying a very narrow portion of the spectrum (typically $\text{BFR} < 0.0001$). Often associated with technological origins as natural sources rarely produce such spectrally confined emissions. These signals are particularly interesting in SETI research.

GeomagStatus: Major Storm.definition: Indicates intense solar-induced geomagnetic activity with Kp index ≥ 7. During such conditions, ionospheric perturbations significantly affect radio observations below 100 MHz, aurora may be visible at mid-latitudes, and satellite communications may experience disruptions.

CIP Classification Label.description: Three-tier rating system for evaluating signal coherence against intelligent transmission criteria.
CIP Classification Label.definition: Classification labels: 'Coherent Information Pattern Detected' ($\text{SSM} > 0.8$, $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.4-0.8, and $\text{ModIndex} > 0.5$), 'Potential Information Pattern' ($\text{SSM} > 0.6$ and $\text{EntropyVal}$ between 0.3-0.9$), or 'No Clear Pattern' (all other signals).

SigClassType: Broadband Transient.description: Illustrates a class of brief signals covering wide frequency ranges.
SigClassType: Broadband Transient.definition: Describes short-duration signals ($\text{SigDurSec}$ typically $< 5$) that span a large portion of the spectrum ($\text{BFR} > 0.1$). Examples include solar radio bursts, lightning discharges, and certain types of cosmic explosions like Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs).

PolarMode: Circular.description: Illustrates circular polarization in detected signals.
PolarMode: Circular.definition: Describes electromagnetic waves where the electric field vector rotates in a circular pattern as the wave propagates. Circular polarization maintaining high purity across frequency (indicated by $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$ stability) is rare in natural sources and may indicate technological origin.

EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.description: Illustrates characteristics suggesting deliberate signal encoding.
EncryptEvid: Strong Pattern.definition: Indicates detection of non-random, internally consistent patterns that resist simple decoding but show hallmarks of designed encryption or encoding. Characterized by high $\text{EntropyVal} (> 0.7)$ combined with structural regularity that defies natural explanation.

EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.description: Illustrates a sophisticated encoding method used in telecommunications.
EncodeType: Frequency Hopping.definition: Describes a transmission technique where the signal rapidly switches frequencies according to a predetermined sequence. Detection would be characterized by discontinuous spectral features that follow a pattern. This technique is used on Earth to secure communications and reduce interference.

FalsePosProb: <0.01.description: Illustrates extremely high confidence in signal detection.
FalsePosProb: <0.01.definition: Indicates less than 1% probability that the signal is a false detection or artifact. Such low false positive probability typically results from multiple independent confirmations, excellent signal strength (high $\text{SnrRatio}$), and elimination of all known terrestrial and instrumental sources.

Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).description: Quantifies the sophistication of signal modulation based on type and stability.
Modulation Complexity Score (MCS).definition: $\text{MCS} = \text{ModIndex} \times (1 + \text{SSM}) \times M_{\text{factor}}$, where $M_{\text{factor}}$ is 2 for $\text{ModType} = \text{'AM'}$, 1.5 for 'FM', and 1 for other types. Incorporates Signal Stability Metric (SSM) to weight stable modulations higher.

Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.description: Calculates likelihood of artificial intelligence origin based on encoding complexity and technosignature indicators.
Artificial Intelligence Detection Probab.definition: $\text{AIDP} = \frac{\text{ECI} \times \text{TOLS}}{1 + \text{NatSrcProb}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) and TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) are weighted against natural source probability.

Observation Quality Factor (OQF).description: Provides a comprehensive measure of observational conditions quality.
Observation Quality Factor (OQF).definition: $\text{OQF} = \text{AOI} \times (1 - \text{LIF}) \times (\text{PointAccArc} < 2 ? 1 : \frac{2}{\text{PointAccArc}})$, where AOI (Atmospheric Observability Index) and LIF (Lunar Interference Factor) are combined with telescope pointing accuracy.

Information Entropy Ratio (IER).description: Compares signal entropy to expected natural background entropy.
Information Entropy Ratio (IER).definition: $\text{IER} = \frac{\text{EntropyVal}}{\text{NatSrcProb} \times 0.9 + 0.1}$, where values significantly greater than 1 suggest non-natural information content. Uses NatSrcProb as a baseline for expected natural entropy.

Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.description: Evaluates the computational efficiency of signal processing relative to complexity.
Signal Processing Efficiency Index (SPEI.definition: $\text{SPEI} = \frac{\text{DecodeIters} \times \text{ProcTimeHrs}}{\text{ECI} \times \text{ComplexIdx}}$, where ECI (Encoding Complexity Index) provides the complexity component to normalize processing time and iterations.

Celestial Location Significance Factor (.description: Calculates significance of signal source location based on astronomical targets of interest.
Celestial Location Significance Factor (.definition: $\text{CLSF} = (\text{CelestObj} ? 2 : 1) \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Giant'} \&\& \text{ObjMassSol} \text{ between } 0.8 \text{ and } 1.2 ? 1.5 : 1) \times (\text{ObjMetal} > 0 ? \text{ObjMetal} + 1 : 0.5)$, where higher values indicate source locations more likely to harbor intelligent life.

Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).description: Quantifies overall confidence in signal verification across multiple parameters.
Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS).definition: $\text{CCS} = (1 - \text{FalsePosProb}) \times \text{DecodeConf} \times \text{ClassConf} \times (\text{SNQI} > 0 ? \frac{\text{SNQI}}{10} + 0.5 : 0.1)$, where SNQI (Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator) provides a quality weighting factor.

Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).description: Assesses signal relevance based on source's position in habitable zone.
Habitable Zone Signal Relevance (HZSR).definition: $\text{HZSR} = \text{TOLS} \times (\text{ObjType} == \text{'Dwarf'} ? (0.7 \leq \text{ObjMassSol} \leq 1.4 ? (0.8 \leq \frac{\text{SourceDistLy}}{\sqrt{\text{ObjMassSol}}} \leq 1.7 ? 2 : 0.5) : 0.3) : 0.1)$, where TOLS (Technological Origin Likelihood Score) is weighted by stellar habitability factors.

Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).description: Measures confidence in identified signal patterns based on multiple factors.
Pattern Recognition Confidence (PRC).definition: $\text{PRC} = (\text{RepeatCount} > 1 ? 1 + \log_{10}(\text{RepeatCount}) : 0.5) \times (\text{EntropyVal} < 0.9 ? 1 : 0.3) \times \text{SCR}$, where SCR (Signal Complexity Ratio) provides complexity weighting.

NTM Classification System.description: A tiered classification system for Narrowband Technological Markers based on signal characteristics.
NTM Classification System.definition: Three-tier classification: 'Strong NTM' (BFR < 0.0001 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.1 AND non-natural modulation), 'Moderate NTM' (BFR < 0.0005 AND FreqDriftHzs < 0.5 AND non-natural modulation), and 'Not NTM' (all other signals).

High-Confidence Technosignature.description: Defines signals with extremely high likelihood of technological origin.
High-Confidence Technosignature.definition: A Technosignature with $\text{CCS} > 0.9$, $\text{MCS} > 1.5$, and $\text{AIDP} > 0.8$, indicating a signal that meets the basic Technosignature criteria with additional confirmation through modulation complexity and artificial intelligence detection markers.

Habitable Zone Transmission.description: Identifies signals originating from stellar habitable zones with technological characteristics.
Habitable Zone Transmission.definition: A signal with $\text{HZSR} > 1.5$ and Technosignature characteristics, originating from a star system with conditions potentially suitable for life, making it a priority candidate for SETI research.

Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.description: Identifies signal patterns consistent with sophisticated communication protocols.
Multi-Channel Communication Protocol.definition: Signal exhibiting Coherent Information Pattern (CIP) characteristics across multiple frequency channels with coordinated timing ($\text{RepeatCount} > 3$, $\text{PeriodSec}$ consistent across observations) and $\text{ECI} > 2.0$, suggesting a designed communication system.

Quantum-Coherent Transmission.description: Describes signals potentially employing quantum properties for communication.
Quantum-Coherent Transmission.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ containing 'Significant' or 'Observed' patterns, exhibiting unusually high information density ($\text{InfoDense} > 1.5$) while maintaining an $\text{ECI} > 2.5$, suggesting advanced transmission technologies beyond conventional radiofrequency methods.

Research Critical Signal.description: Defines signals requiring immediate and extensive scientific resources.
Research Critical Signal.definition: Signals meeting Target of Opportunity (TOO) criteria with additional $\text{PRC} > 0.8$ and $\text{IMDF} < 0.5$, indicating high-quality, minimally distorted signals that show recognizable patterns warranting priority allocation of research resources.

Directed Transmission.description: Identifies signals that appear specifically directed rather than omnidirectional.
Directed Transmission.definition: Signals with high spatial stability ($\text{SpatStab} = \text{'Moderate'}$), narrow beam characteristics ($\text{PolarMode} = \text{'Linear'}$ with stable $\text{PolarAngleDeg}$), and high $\text{TOLS} > 0.85$, suggesting intentional transmission toward our location.

Signal of Galactic Significance.description: Classifies signals with potential importance to galactic civilization models.
Signal of Galactic Significance.definition: Signals originating from regions of high $\text{CLSF} (> 2.0)$ that display Technosignature characteristics and have $\text{AIDP} > 0.7$, representing potential evidence of advanced civilizations at galactic-relevant locations.

CCS Approximation.description: Simplified CCS calculation using direct signal-to-noise ratio values when full Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator (SNQI) data is unavailable.

Observation-Verified Signal.description: Defines signals that have undergone rigorous verification processes.
Observation-Verified Signal.definition: Signals observed under Optimal Observing Window (OOW) conditions with $\text{OQF} > 0.85$ and $\text{CCS} > 0.8$, indicating high-quality observations with multiple verification methods applied.

Anomalous Quantum Signal.description: Describes signals exhibiting quantum properties inconsistent with current physics models.
Anomalous Quantum Signal.definition: Signals with $\text{QuantEffects}$ indicating anomalous behavior, $\text{AnomScore} > 8$, and unusually high $\text{MCS} (> 2.0)$, suggesting either unknown natural quantum phenomena or extremely advanced transmission technologies beyond current human capabilities.

Analyzable Signals.definition: Signals with SNQI > 0 are considered analyzable.

Bandwidth-to-Frequency Ratio (BFR).definition: $\text{BFR} = \frac{\text{BwHz}}{\text{CenterFreqMhz} \times 1{,}000{,}000}$, used to characterize signal spread relative to its frequency band.

TOLS Category.description: Classification of signals based on TOLS thresholds.
TOLS Category.definition: Categorized as 'Low' if TOLS < 0.25, 'Medium' if TOLS < 0.75, and 'High' otherwise.

High Confidence Signals.description: Signal with Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) > 0.8, indicating high reliability.

Equipment Problems.definition: A telescope is considered to have an equipment problem whenever **any** of its key subsystem states are not in their nominal condition: • Equipment status is not “Operational”; • Calibration status is not “Current”; • Cooling-system status is not “Normal”.

WITH station_aoi AS (
